title: docs(spec): the span auto clause names the field types the form renderer really widens
body:
Fixes #18516

Clause-②: no

## The defect

`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` — `FormField.span`, the `'auto'` clause — shipped this sentence to authors:

> wide widgets **"like textarea/richtext/json/file/subform take the whole row"**

Three of those five names are wrong, and two types that really are wide went unnamed. An author reads that sentence to decide how to lay out a form.

## Re-derived on this tree — not inherited from the card

Both falsifications were re-measured here against objectui at the `.objectui-sha` pin `53ded82bf7`, by **executing** that tree's own code: `git show PIN:packages/plugin-form/src/autoLayout.ts` verbatim, plus lines 2472-2521 of `git show PIN:packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx` (`pickSpanClass`, extracted verbatim by line range, 50 lines, sha256 recorded) wrapped in a driver that supplies the `containerClass` the pin's own `CONTAINER_GRID_COLS` produces.

### 1. `WIDE_FIELD_TYPES` is ten entries, and the three named types are in none of them

`packages/plugin-form/src/autoLayout.ts:57` at the pin, exactly:

```
field:textarea   field:markdown   field:html   field:grid   field:richtext
textarea         markdown         html         grid         richtext
```

The `plugin-detail` twin at `autoLayout.ts:53` carries the same ten in a different order.

Executed — `span: 'auto'` (key omitted), 3-column grid, at the pin:

**Swept along the RUNTIME path** — `mapFieldTypeToFormType` → `isWideFieldType` → `resolveColSpan` → `pickSpanClass`. ⚠️ The BARE path (`isWideFieldType(specName)`, which is what objectui's own pin test measures) answers four; every site assigning `FormField.type` at the pin maps first, and `repeater` reaches the wide widget only along the mapped path. That difference is what round 1 missed.

| type | `isWideFieldType` | `resolveColSpan` | class emitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `textarea` | true | 3 | `@2xl:col-span-3` |
| `markdown` | true | 3 | `@2xl:col-span-3` |
| `html` | true | 3 | `@2xl:col-span-3` |
| `richtext` | true | 3 | `@2xl:col-span-3` |
| `json` | **false** | **1** | *(none)* |
| `file` | **false** | **1** | *(none)* |
| `subform` | **false** | **1** | *(none)* |
| `text` — narrow control | false | 1 | *(none)* |
| `repeater` | **true** — maps to `field:grid` | **3** | `@2xl:col-span-3` |
| `field:textarea` — widget-id control | true | 3 | `@2xl:col-span-3` |

Swept across the whole `FieldType` vocabulary (**49** members, two instruments agreeing — the executed `FieldType.options` and the enum source tokens with comments stripped), the runtime-path wide set is **exactly five**: `textarea`, `markdown`, `html`, `richtext` and `repeater`. ⚠️ objectui's own pin test asserts the **bare-path four**, and that assertion is true of the bare path — it is not the path an authored field takes.

**Every zero reading carries a firing control.** The three full-row decision sites at the pin are `plugin-form/src/autoLayout.ts`, `plugin-detail/src/autoLayout.ts` and `app-shell/.../studio-design/formFieldType.ts`. Searching them for `json` / `file` / `subform` as type literals: **0** in each. Control `textarea` in the same three files: **2 / 2 / 0** — the third is a mapper, not a decision site, which is why it reads zero on the control too. Wider control: `col-span-full` under `packages/*/src/*` at the pin is **15** hits (section dividers in `form.tsx:61`, dashboard wrappers, and the designer canvas) — the instrument fires, and none of the 15 is a field-type path for any of the three names.

### 2. The tier claim, and why the fix must not flip its sign

`resolveColSpan` returns a **cell count**, not a class. The class comes from `pickSpanClass`, which picks the first breakpoint whose column count reaches the target:

```
CONTAINER_GRID_COLS[3] = 'grid gap-4 grid-cols-1 @md:grid-cols-2 @2xl:grid-cols-3'
matches = [ @md -> 2, @2xl -> 3 ]
find(cols >= 3)  ->  @2xl   =>   '@2xl:col-span-3'
```

So at the `@md` tier the grid is two columns and the wide field carries **no span class at all** — one cell of two, not the row. Probe row, executed: `textarea`, `span: 'auto'`, 3-column grid, at the pin, class `@2xl:col-span-3`, 1 of 2 at `@md`. A replacement sentence promising a whole row at every tier would be exactly as false as the one being replaced, so the clause states the resolved **column count** and leaves the tier sentence beside it to say how far down the tiers that span is emitted.

## What the clause says now

Before:

> the renderer sizes the field from its widget type × the current column count (wide widgets like textarea/richtext/json/file/subform take the whole row) … at the `.objectui-sha` pin `53ded82bf7` only the widest tier's class is emitted …

After:

> Relative field width. 'auto' (default — omit it): the renderer sizes the field from its widget type × the current column count — at the pin this repo builds against (`.objectui-sha` = `53ded82bf7`), only textarea, markdown, html, richtext and repeater resolve to the full column count (repeater reaches it through the wide `field:grid` widget it maps to). 'full': resolves to the form grid's full column count. How far down the container-query tiers that span is emitted is the renderer's, not this key's: at that same pin only the widest tier's class is emitted (`@2xl:col-span-3` for a 3-column grid), so at intermediate widths the field takes a single cell, not the row (one of two at the 720px modal width; measured in Chromium at viewport widths 390, 720 and 1700).

One `.describe()` string, one line of diff in `src`.

## The guard — #18508's asserting spelling, and why it applies

The card notes this sentence goes stale at the bump absorbing objectui `bd09957380`, which emits one clamped class per multi-column tier. `check:objectui-pin-citations` (#18508) distinguishes two spellings: an **asserting** citation (`` `.objectui-sha` = `SHA` ``) claims *this is the pin we build against* and is compared against the pin file, while a **historical** one (`` `.objectui-sha` pin `SHA` ``) is a dated record and is never checked.

The clause was carrying the historical spelling while making a claim about today — that is precisely the silent-rot state the gate exists to end — so the citation moves to the asserting form, and the two pin-sensitive halves (the wide-type list and the tier behaviour) now sit under one citation, the second referring to it as "that same pin" so there is one citation, not two.

**Reverse-verified, both legs, fix committed first, mutation proven on disk by `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`:**

| leg | mutation | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| guard | asserting citation's sha to `1a2b3c4d5e6` | RED | **RED**, exit 1, `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts:2925 cites 1a2b3c4d5e6` |
| control | same wrong sha, in the **historical** spelling | GREEN — the old spelling buys no guard | **GREEN**, exit 0, 26 asserting / 46 historical |

The control leg is the argument for the spelling change: with a plainly wrong sha, the spelling this clause used to carry passes. Both legs restored under a `trap`, each restore proven by blob hash (`cd5a238e1930` == HEAD) with `git diff HEAD` empty. The gate reads `packages/spec/src` directly, so `dist` is not on its path and no dist preflight applies.

Gate after the change: **27 asserting** citations match the pin (was 26), **45 historical** (was 46) — exactly the one citation converted, nothing else moved.

## Population the one string moves — re-derived

The card measured `src` 1 · `dist` 30 · `json-schema` 12 · docs 2 — ⚠️ that last figure is a **file** count. Re-derived on this tree for the **new** string, with the unit stated: `src` **1 file / 1 occurrence** · `dist` **30 / 30** · `json-schema` **12 files / 22 occurrences** · `content/docs/references/ui/view.mdx` **2 occurrences**. The retired wording is gone from the tree with one deliberate exception: the changeset **quotes the original sentence**, which is a historical record by construction. ⛔ The earlier phrasing of this line — that zero occurrences remain anywhere outside `.git` — is withdrawn as over-claimed.

`check:generated` proved exactly one artifact stale (`content/docs/references/**`) and `--fix` regenerated only that one; `check:authorable-surface`, `check:api-surface` and `check:api-surface-declarations` all stayed green — the last because it excludes leading TSDoc by design, so a re-worded describe does not churn it.

## Changeset — owed, and why

`@objectstack/spec` ships `dist`, `json-schema` **and** `src/**/*.zod.ts` in its `files[]`, so all three of the moved populations are published bytes. A `patch` changeset is owed and is in this PR; `skip-changeset` would be wrong here.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` — green (under the shared verify lock).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` — green.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` — **500 files / 14632 tests passed**.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` — green after regenerating the one stale artifact.
- Gate families from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: **100 derived, 94 run green, 6 NOT MEASURED, 0 unrun** — reconciled with `--ran` (exit 0), every line carrying its exit code captured before any pipe.
- The 6 NOT MEASURED all refused with their own stated prerequisite — they read **built** output of packages outside this change's dependency closure (`@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/client-react`, `@objectstack/objectql`, and in one case most of the monorepo). `packages/spec` has no workspace dependencies, so the closure build is an empty run and those builds are CI's farm: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` (exit 3), `check:doc-security-posture` (exit 3), `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:skill-examples` (exit 1, needs `client-react` built), `pnpm check:docs-transcript-drift` (exit 3), `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3), `pnpm check:lean-entry-closure` (exit 3). Exit 3 is this repo's "nothing was measured" code — neither a pass nor a finding.

## Scope

Triage's fence, verbatim and binding:

> ⚠️ 边界:改的是**那一句**。⛔ 不要顺手去改渲染器的 `WIDE_FIELD_TYPES` —— 那是扩大接受集,是另一类改动、另一张卡。

`WIDE_FIELD_TYPES` and every other objectui file were **read only** — no renderer behaviour is touched, and nothing here widens an accept set. No key, default, enum member or exported name moves: the same authored metadata is accepted and refused before and after, which is what `Clause-②: no` declares.

## Acceptance notes

- `noted, not filed` — the docblock above `span` (`view.zod.ts` ~2914-2924) carries its own citation of the same pin in the historical spelling plus the prose reminder *"re-read this block at the pin bump that absorbs it"*. It states nothing false today and is not an authored-metadata trap, so it is not one of the three filing classes. It is left untouched deliberately: the describe's asserting citation now reds on the adjacent line at the next bump, and whoever re-reads it has the docblock in front of them. Successor: the pin-bump PR that absorbs objectui `bd09957380`.
- `noted, not filed` — the two `WIDE_FIELD_TYPES` sets in objectui (`plugin-form` and `plugin-detail`) are maintained as byte-equal twins by hand, with no cross-repo pin holding them equal; `richtextSurfaceParity.test.tsx` compares the two exported predicates rather than the sets. Nothing is wrong today. Successor: none in this repo — it is an objectui-side observation, and this card's fence forbids touching those files.

The contract review of record on the previous head (`cee5969dee`) returned FAIL on one finding — the clause was false in the other direction, because `repeater` maps to the wide `field:grid` widget — and the sections above are updated to the runtime-path measurement. Two counts the review corrected are fixed here: the `FieldType` population is **49**, not 55, and the json-schema figure is **12 files / 22 occurrences**, not 12 occurrences. The round-1 claim that no occurrence of the retired wording remains anywhere is withdrawn: the changeset quotes the original sentence, by construction. The implementer named all of these edits in its report and correctly declined to patch this body itself — a dev writes a PR body once, at the POST that opens it.</sub>
